task.description: Hard-gate CODE-DESIGNER's ISS-0480 remedy design (revert secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs to async:false) against: mechanism soundness, INV-1's empirical truth, any other mode-flipping path, the unconfirmed PackUpdateMigrationTest FK symptom, the ISS-0423 cost/tension honesty, the verification plan's ability to distinguish fixed from lucky, and INV-1's lack of enforcement.

result.summary:
VERDICT: PASS. This is a correctly-scoped, honestly-argued two-file revert with a mechanism traced to real source (manager.ex:163-170, confirmed by direct read), and I independently re-derived every empirical claim the fix depends on rather than trusting the design's or Step 1's prose. No blocking gap found. One new fact surfaced during verification that the design did not discuss, but it does not change the verdict -- documented below as a MINOR finding for the record, not a rework trigger.

===== ITEM 1: DOES THE REMEDY CLOSE THE HOLE? INV-1 CHECKED EMPIRICALLY, NOT INHERITED =====

Independently re-ran the design's own §1.3 anchored count: `grep -rl "^\s*use.*async: true" test --include=*.exs | wc -l` -> 66. Matches the design's own re-derived figure exactly (not merely copied -- I ran it myself, output above).

Then went further than the design's own §4.1 check, which only greps for the literal string `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo`/`Sandbox.mode(Repo)` in each file. I additionally checked (a) every file matching that grep for its own async declaration, (b) every one of the 51 real `provisioned_tenant!` callers (a superset, since a caller reaches `Sandbox.mode/2` indirectly without the literal string appearing in its own file) for async status, and (c) every one of the 66 async:true files for any textual reference to `provisioned_tenant!`/`Sandbox.mode`/`TenantFixture.`.

Result: exactly TWO real hits across all three angles -- `test/letflow/secrets_test.exs` and `test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs` -- matching the design's claim precisely. Two additional textual matches were investigated and confirmed to be FALSE POSITIVES, same class as the design's own already-disclosed `store_test.exs`/`authorization_ac9_test.exs` false positives:
  - `test/support/tenant_slug_test.exs` (async: true) -- its moduledoc mentions `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` only when describing OTHER, historical pre-fix files' behavior; its own test body spawns separate `elixir -e` OS processes and never touches `Letflow.Repo` at all.
  - `test/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config_test.exs` (async: true) -- its own moduledoc explicitly documents why it does NOT call `provisioned_tenant!/1` (touches only the global `tenants` table via plain `Repo.insert!` under DataCase's own transaction; the one string match is prose contrasting itself with `identity_test.exs`). Confirmed via `grep -n "provisioned_tenant!\|Sandbox\.mode\|TenantFixture\."` against the file body: only the moduledoc line, no real call.

CONCLUSION: INV-1 holds, verified empirically by me independently, not inherited from Step 1 or CODE-DESIGNER's own count.

===== ITEM 2: ANY OTHER MODE-FLIPPING PATH? A NEW FACT FOUND, DOES NOT CHANGE THE VERDICT =====

Checked test_helper.exs and every file under test/support/ for `Sandbox.mode` calls beyond data_case.ex and tenant_fixture.ex, which the design's §0/§1.3 do not enumerate exhaustively. Found two the design never mentions:
  - `test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex`'s `sweep_orphans/2` calls `Sandbox.mode(repo, :auto)` then `:manual` in an `after` block -- but this runs ONLY before `ExUnit.start()` and via `ExUnit.after_suite/1` (confirmed: its own moduledoc states this and `test/test_helper.exs` is its only production call site among the four grep hits), i.e. strictly outside the async-phase window entirely -- both boundary points are guaranteed-empty-running-set moments per its own documented design (ISS-0064). Not a hazard: it never runs concurrently with any async test.
  - `test/support/tenant_template.ex`'s `ensure_template!/0` also calls `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` unconditionally, and IS called from `provisioned_tenant!/1` (tenant_fixture.ex:356, via `provision_schema!/2`) for the default `template: :clone` path -- i.e. every one of the 46 TenantFixture call sites, not just the two culprits, triggers a SECOND `Sandbox.mode(:auto)` request per provisioning. Checked whether this is a fifth mechanism: it is not, because both calls request the identical mode (`:auto`) in the same call chain with nothing else running between them for that same process, so the second call hits DBConnection's own `%{mode: mode} = state` no-op guard (manager.ex:163-164) and never reaches the disruptive check-in-all branch a second time. Checked the two other direct callers of `TenantTemplate.ensure_template!/0` outside `provisioned_tenant!/1` (`test/support/tenant_template_test.exs`, `test/support/tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs`) -- both `async: false`. No new exposure path.

CONCLUSION: no other mode-flipping path threatens the fix. This is disclosed as a MINOR documentation gap in the design (§0 does not mention `tenant_schema_reaper.ex`/`tenant_template.ex` at all, even to rule them out) rather than a defect in the remedy -- the design's conclusion is still correct, it just didn't show its work on two files a careful reader might reasonably ask about. Not a blocker: the design's own §1.3 explicitly scopes INV-1 to 'no async:true file may call Sandbox.mode/2', and I independently confirmed that scope is exhaustive over the real call graph, not merely over the design's own enumerated file list.

===== ITEM 3: THE SECOND SYMPTOM (PackUpdateMigrationTest FK) =====

Read the actual test body and `lib/letflow/row_approval.ex`. Confirmed the mechanism is structurally plausible for both symptoms: `RowApprovalTest`'s `Repo.update_all` pattern-matches `{1, _}` (row_approval.ex:85-87) -- exactly consistent with Step 1's observed `{0, nil}` failure if the connection was swapped between a preceding read and this write. `PackUpdateMigrationTest`'s own moduledoc (lines 1-30) confirms it inserts into a real FK-constrained global table (`tenants.id` via `solution_pack_artefact_bases.tenant_id`) and deliberately does NOT use TenantFixture -- a pure bystander with the same DataCase-unconditional-checkout shape as RowApprovalTest. The design's mechanism-level argument (table-touched is irrelevant; per-connection discard is what matters; both are bystanders with no other explanatory code path) is sound and is not merely asserted -- Step 1 already ruled out the shared-table theory directly, and the design correctly declines to inflate 0/4 non-reproduction into false confidence, naming exactly what would overturn it (a future repro on the fixed branch). The design's disposition (ship covering both by mechanism, disclose the asymmetry, don't hold the fix hostage to an already-rare repro) is proportionate and honestly framed, not evasive.

===== ITEM 4: THE ISS-0423 TENSION =====

The design's refusal to fabricate a precise suite-level wall-clock number is honest, not evasive: it explicitly states why (BEFORE/AFTER spreads of +281s/+354s across nominally-identical ISS-0423 runs already dwarf what 2-of-66 files' async status could contribute) and gives the one number it CAN support precisely (async-file count reverts from 66 to 64). I considered whether a cheap isolated timing check (these 2 files alone, async vs sync) would strengthen the argument, and concluded it would not answer the actually-relevant question: ISS-0423's throughput goal is total suite wall-clock under shared `max_cases` scheduling, and an isolated 2-file timing diff does not measure that -- it would produce a number that looks precise but doesn't bear on the real trade-off, which is exactly the kind of fabricated-precision the design correctly declines to manufacture. The qualitative argument (a MAJOR 75%-hit-rate bystander-test intermittent costs more in pipeline rework/trust than a low-single-digit-percent share of an already-small lever, with the two dominant ISS-0423 levers -- parallelism 2.9x, template-clone 4.9x/provisioning -- both untouched) is proportionate. PASS on this item; not inflated to a rework demand for a number that would not actually inform the decision.

===== ITEM 5: VERIFICATION PLAN =====

Section 4 explicitly rejects a single green run as evidence (quoting core-directives.md's own re-derivation principle) and requires BOTH a structural proof (the §4.1 grep, which I re-ran myself and got a materially different raw row count than the design's own prose -- see finding below) AND a 4+-seed empirical stress run using Step 1's own proven-reproducing recipe (the full async-cohort file set, not a diluted plain `mix test`), with an explicit 0-tolerance failure bar on the two named tests. This is capable of distinguishing 'fixed' from 'got lucky': the structural check is a mechanism-level proof (if zero async:true files call Sandbox.mode/2, the disruptive check-in cannot fire during the async phase, independent of seed or scheduling), and the seed-varying stress run is specifically designed to perturb the race window Step 1's own diagnosis found sensitive to scheduling order. This is not a MAJOR gap -- it is the opposite of leaning on a single clean run.

FINDING (MINOR, non-blocking): I re-ran the design's own §4.1 command verbatim and got 76 rows, not the 75 the design's prose states; the raw `grep -rl` file count (before the `use Letflow.DataCase`-anchoring filter that command applies) is 79, and 3 of those files use `ExUnit.Case` rather than `Letflow.DataCase` and are silently dropped by the command's own filter (their existence is not disclosed in the design's prose). None of this affects the safety-relevant number, which I independently re-verified three separate ways to be exactly 2 async:true callers, matching the design's claim precisely -- this is a miscount in an illustrative total, not in the number the fix's correctness actually depends on. Recorded so TEST-RUNNER/ELIXIR-DEV does not report a mismatch as a surprise when they run §4.1 for real and get 76 rather than 75.

===== ITEM 6: INV-1 ENFORCEMENT =====

Confirmed directly: `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex` gates only on the ISS-0069 warning substring; no lint task or compile-time check for Sandbox.mode-under-async exists anywhere in `lib/mix/tasks/`. The design's §6 disclosure (prose-only invariant, a future silent violation is possible, recommend a follow-on lint wired into `mix letflow.check`) is accurate and appropriately scoped as a follow-on rather than a same-run blocker -- INV-1 is trivially true TODAY by construction (zero callers after the revert), and the risk is entirely about a FUTURE agent violating it without reading this record, which is a real but genuinely separately-sized concern matching this project's own established pattern (ISS-0428/ISS-0427 were split out of ISS-0423 the same way). Not a reason to hold this fix.

===== OVERALL =====

The remedy is genuinely sound and honestly scoped: a real mechanism (confirmed by me at the source), a correctly narrow blast radius (2 files, 0 lib/ changes), an accurately re-derived safety invariant (66 async files, exactly 2 real Sandbox.mode/2 callers among them, verified via three independent angles including two the design itself did not check), an honest disclosure of the unconfirmed second symptom, a proportionate and non-evasive cost argument for reversing ISS-0423's own win, a verification plan that actually distinguishes fixed-from-lucky, and an honest disclosure of INV-1's current lack of enforcement. PASS.

issues.description: Design §0 does not mention or rule out test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex and test/support/tenant_template.ex, both of which also call Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo/repo, ...). I independently verified neither threatens the fix (the reaper runs only at guaranteed-empty suite boundaries; the template's ensure_template!/0 call is reached from provisioned_tenant!/1 itself and only ever re-requests the same already-current mode, hitting DBConnection's no-op guard, plus its two other direct callers are both async: false) -- but a future reader auditing this design in isolation would have to re-derive this themselves, since the design's own §0/§1.3 enumerate only data_case.ex and tenant_fixture.ex as Sandbox.mode/2 call sites. Recommend CODE-DESIGNER or a follow-on note add one sentence naming these two files and why they're out of scope, so the next auditor doesn't have to re-find them from scratch.

Design §4.1's own verification command, re-run verbatim by me, returns 76 rows on this branch tip, not the 75 the design's prose states; the unfiltered grep -rl count is 79, and 3 files (test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs, test/letflow/sandbox_pool_call_timeout_test.exs, test/support/tenant_slug_test.exs -- all use ExUnit.Case, not Letflow.DataCase) are silently excluded by the command's own `use Letflow.DataCase` anchor and never disclosed as excluded. The safety-relevant number (exactly 2 async:true callers) is correct and independently reconfirmed by me via three separate methods -- this is a cosmetic miscount in an illustrative total figure, not a defect in the remedy's correctness. Flagging so TEST-RUNNER/ELIXIR-DEV running §4.1 for real does not mistake the 75-vs-76 mismatch for a regression.
